notes.detail: Returned credential permissions are unknown; effective permissions were not tested.
Administrative checks cover current super-administrator flags and supported direct or indirect role assignments. Group membership paths and effective permissions were not tested.
Domain-wide delegation inventory is not assessed. Review Security → Access and data control → API controls → Manage Domain Wide Delegation in the Admin console.

2-step verification checks read Google's current per-account enforcement and enrollment flags. Organizational-unit policy, grace periods, configuration groups, sign-in through another identity provider, verification methods, backup codes and phishing resistance were not assessed.

Google reports that every active account in this Workspace (5 active accounts) is currently required to use 2-step verification. You did not say who must use it; declare it under access.mfa in the engagement file.

Third-party app access was not checked: the selected Workspace profile does not read it. The check lists apps people allowed into their mail, Drive or calendar, a common way an attacker keeps access after a phishing email. It needs the Workspace permission admin.directory.user.security, which Google offers only together with the ability to revoke app access, sign people out and turn off 2-step verification; the checks above do not need it. If your organization wants this check, an administrator can approve a dedicated credential for it, so the everyday one keeps read-only permissions; then run again with SCHECK_WORKSPACE_PROFILE=directory_oauth_mail.

Mail forwarding was not read: it needs a Google service account with domain-wide delegation, and the credential file this run used (the one GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS names, or your own gcloud sign-in) holds one person's sign-in, which scheck does not use to read mail settings. To turn the check on, ask whoever manages your Google setup (often your IT provider) to create a service account with domain-wide delegation for gmail.readonly, or leave the check off. Nothing else in this run was affected.

Mail forwarding settings were read whole for 0 of 5 active mailboxes; not read whole: admin@example.com (super administrator, not attempted), carol@example.com (not attempted), dan@example.com (not attempted), erin@example.com (not attempted), eve@example.com (not attempted). Check those mailboxes' forwarding and filters by hand in each person's Gmail settings. Not attempted, because not active or without a mailbox: 1 suspended. Checked: automatic forwarding and forwarding filters of each active mailbox, by destination domain. Not checked: whether any message was forwarded, what each filter matches, the Admin console's forwarding setting, routing and compliance rules, mail delegates, POP/IMAP and other mail apps, send-as addresses, where mail forwarded to a group or another address in your domains goes next, and suspended or archived mailboxes. To see what was actually forwarded, use Email Log Search in the Admin console.
